LESSON: CITIZENSHIP

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: Political Systems
Topic 4.3: Citizenship
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 4

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Citizenship, part of Political Systems in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade six SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How do we demonstrate good citizenship in our country? 2. Why is it important to know our rights and responsibilities as citizens?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Citizenship together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

• Communication and collaboration: A learner acquires listening, reading, writing, speaking and teamwork

skills as they brainstorm on the qualities of a good citizen of Kenya.

• Creativity and imagination: A learner enhance the skill of making connections as they develop posters, charts,

tactile charts or braille cards on values of a good citizen and places them in strategic places in school.
